searchText: Hey! Happy to run that in bloatnet (2x mainnet state size atm). Do you have any set of tests/benchmarks we can run via `execution-specs` or similar? What exactly do you want to get out of this? Metrics like performance? Or IO/bandwidth etc.. ? <@402853454126776320> <@680337202521440470> for SSTORE/SLOAD we already have some results in bloatnet. See: https://grafana.observability.ethpandaops.io/d/fezrrtv924cu8e/opcodes-benchmarking-stateful?orgId=1&from=2025-10-23T07:59:21.152Z&to=2025-10-23T10:51:04.491Z&timezone=browser&var-posgreSQL=benuragv7iuwwb&var-ClientName=$__all&var-TestTitle=$__all&refresh=auto Soon to have a lot more data and test cases! Great! Gary has a reference to his code in his post. Best we'd just re-run it with bloatnet attached. It's not EELS tests but more low level tests on parallelizing ssd access on Ethereum data ^ thats the post Continuing the discussion during yesterday's breakout on adding `gas_used` values into the BAL, I tried modelling it here: https://hackmd.io/@Nerolation/HJe-yyc1Zl It's true that the overhead (best case compared to worst-case) will never be worse than 16.67M gas but I think there's still potential in going from ordered list scheduling to greedy scheduling. Will forward with Gary via DM then and get back here with results I dont think it is worth exploring this any more, we are talking about worst case (drop of 25% is parallel exec is nothing if we have 3x reduced the time) of not usual case (one big tx at the end of block). And optimizing this not usual case is not worth imo. It's true that everyday blocks look different but we have to consider the worst-cases here. This means that in the future, to measure worst-case blocks execution times, we need to think in the realms of "ordered list scheduling" vs "greedy scheduling" with the latter being simpler to reason about. Where are the 25% from? In my model it's 39% at 8 cores and a gas limit of 300M. 25% for 60M block and 16M tx. Optimal number of gas on 300M block on 8 cores is 37.5M, this is 8x the speed up worst case if one core is 53.5 (37.5+16) this is still 5.6x speedup. Optional number of gas on 300M block on 4 cores, is 75M, this is 4x the speed up worst ase if on one core is 91M (75+16) this is 3.2x I see! Wouldn't you say going from 8x to 5.6x is a quite significant drop that limits further scaling as we focus on worst-cases? It is big, maybe it will be good to consider, but speeding up verification by 8x does not help with building of block, and this factor is not going to be exact with all that is happening on one machine, having leeway is maybe good. true but for local builders nothing would get worse at least and those that have the resources to build that big blocks would probably be happy if we let them. Agree, we need leeway but this feels like we're leaving potential on the table. I tend to agree with you <@429719902363058177> . Especially since the worst-cases under "greedy + reordering" is not significantly better, it might just nbe worth it. I still need to think about it more, but here’s how it looks so far: If we assume homogeneous node hardware (same number of cores; which might be overly unrealistic already) and validators gradually raise the gas limit to fully exploit greedy scheduling with reordering, we can achieve around 87.5% efficiency gains. If we can actually leverage that, not sure. In contrast, with ordered-list scheduling, the worst-case execution time scales linearly with the block gas limit - which might be nice, even though it might leave some efficiency potential on the table. When calculating how much smaller it is, it made me thinking, it is still the edge case, would assume there is not a lot of 16M transactions out there. It made me change my stance and wouldn't be this strong agains it, maybe it is just adding it in one of follow up forks, just so people have time to explore how much is it needed.

Continuing the discussion during yesterday's breakout on adding `gas_used` values into the BAL, I tried modelling it here:
https://hackmd.io/@Nerolation/HJe-yyc1Zl

It's true that the overhead (best case compared to worst-case) will never be worse than 16.67M gas but I think there's still potential in going from ordered list scheduling to greedy scheduling.
